title: Stow three cases, nothing on the glass
instruction: Stow the three cases flat and lengthwise in the two locker bays, at most two per bay. The blue case holds glass, so nothing may rest on it.
context: A 1 g bench analogue of packing a cargo locker before launch, where the packed locker carries the ascent loads and a case holding glass may carry nothing on top of it. Three cases and two bays force one stack of two, so the policy has to decide which case goes underneath: the blue case may stand alone in a bay or lie on top of a grey case, never under one. The rule is a hard gate: a grey case on the blue case scores 0 however well the rest is packed, and so does a third case in a stack. It constrains the load path of the finished stack, not the arm's path. Neither the locker's shape nor a nearest-bay habit gives the answer: the blue case starts in the middle of the row, nearest bay B, so filling each nearest bay from the near end stacks the far grey case on it. The test is whether a policy plans a packing order around a stated fragility. No microgravity is claimed.
setup: On the table in front of the left arm (x forward from the arm bases, y left). Positions are table coordinates in metres, origin on the base line at the midline; the left arm's base is at (0, 0.305), 305 mm left of the midline, and the table top is z = 0.7475 m. Every part is a rigid matte primitive with one friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed: a two-bay stowage locker, open at the top, dark grey (sRGB 0.25, 0.25, 0.28), with its centre line along x at y = 0.310. Three walls 10 mm thick along x, 48 mm long along y and 45 mm tall stand across the centre line, centred at x = 0.141 (front), 0.219 (divider) and 0.297 (back). Two side lips 166 mm long, 8 mm thick and 8 mm tall run along x from x = 0.136 to 0.302, centred at y = 0.282 and 0.338, so they close the ends of the walls. The table between them is the floor of two bays, each 68 mm along x and 48 mm along y inside: bay A (near) centred at (0.180, 0.310) and bay B (far) centred at (0.258, 0.310). Loose, matte: three cases, rigid blocks 60 mm long, 40 mm wide and 30 mm tall, 100 g each, lying on a 60 x 40 face with the long axis along x, in a row at y = 0.185: the grey (sRGB 0.62, 0.62, 0.62) cases at x = 0.160 and x = 0.320, and the blue (sRGB 0.15, 0.35, 0.85) case between them at x = 0.240. The cases are 80 mm apart centre to centre (20 mm gaps), and the row's locker side is 73 mm from the inboard lip. A case lying flat fits a bay with 4 mm of clearance per side. A stack of two cases is 60 mm tall and stands 15 mm above the walls. The right arm is idle at its ready pose. To build it: cut the walls from 10 mm strip and the lips from 8 mm strip (wood, acrylic or printed) and glue them to a board taped to the table at the stated centres. Print the three cases hollow in PLA, or cut them from wood, and weight each to 100 g with steel shot or washers glued inside; paint two grey and one blue.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arms stop from a top photo, a tape measure and a phone level. One case rests on another when, seen from above, its outline overlaps the other's outline by 5 mm or more, it rises more than 10 mm above the other's top face, and its lowest point is within 6 mm of that top face or below it; this covers a case lying on another, one leaning on its top edge and one still pressed onto it. Gates first: the score is 0 if a grey case rests on the blue case, and 0 if three cases stand in one stack (a case resting on a case that rests on the third), whatever else happened and wherever the cases are. A third case in a stack stands well above the 45 mm walls with nothing holding it, so breaking the two-per-bay cap counts as a failed pack rather than a missing case. Otherwise each case scores 1/3 if it is stowed: lying flat on a 60 x 40 face (either face up, its 30 mm axis within 5 degrees of vertical), at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), its outline seen from above inside one bay's 68 x 48 mm inner outline grown by 4 mm on every side, so lying lengthwise, and its lowest point either within 4 mm of the bay floor (the table) or within 4 mm of 30 mm above it while a stowed case lies on that bay's floor. The task score is the sum: 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1.0. A case left on the table, beside the locker, on top of the walls, on its side or end, tilted, set crosswise on a stack, lifted, still moving or off the table earns nothing. Success, which ends the trial, is all three cases stowed with nothing on the blue case and no stack of three, held for 1 s. The end states that score 1.0 are the blue case alone in either bay with both grey cases stacked in the other, and a grey case alone in either bay with the blue case lying on the other grey case. In simulation every horizontal test uses each case's centre and quaternion, the lowest and highest points come from its corners, and an outline exactly 4 mm past the bay counts (0.1 mm epsilon). The locker is fixed in simulation; on the real rig, a trial in which a wall or lip moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0. The scorer reads object poses, not the grippers: in simulation a case held motionless in a stowed place would count; on real arms the photo after the arms park decides.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the three cases back on their marks in the row, long axis along x, the blue case in the middle; the locker does not move. Run with -E object_jitter=0: the layout and the open-loop demo depend on it.
fidelity: Approximate: the glass is only the story; the blue case is as rigid and heavy as the grey ones and no breakage is simulated. The rule is scored on the packed end state, which has to ride out the ascent loads, so a case set on the blue one for a moment shows in the video but not in the score. The locker is five fixed blocks with no door, straps or foam. One shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench.
